summary: Defines an XML format for civic location (street addresses) for use in PIDF-LO documents, replacing the format in RFC 4119. It adds elements based on civic types defined for DHCP. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: This is a form for writing down street addresses so computers can pass them around, such as for emergency services.

questions: how to represent civic addresses in xml
what changed in rfc 5139 civic location
how to write a civic address in xml
subtitle: An updated XML format for street addresses in location documents, with more precise road and building elements.

tldr.problem: The civic location format in RFC 4119 lacked parameters needed to specify a street address precisely, such as buildings, rooms and road sections, many of which were already captured for DHCP.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5139 defines a revised XML civicAddress format for PIDF-LO. It adds the civic types from RFC 4776, introduces a hierarchy for road identification, restricts country codes and supports xml:lang.
tldr.outcome: It replaces the civic location format in RFC 4119, so civic addresses in PIDF-LO documents can be more precise and tagged by language.

today: RFC 5139 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4119, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Revise the Civic Format
sections.content:
The original PIDF-LO civic specification in RFC 4119 was found to lack parameters that specify a civic location (a street-address style location) more precisely. Those parameters were largely captured in RFC 4776, the DHCP option for civic addresses.

RFC 5139 revises the GEOPRIV civic form to include them. It also introduces a hierarchical structure for thoroughfare (road) identification, which is used in some countries, and defines new elements for even more precision. The RFC updates RFC 4119 and replaces its civic location format.
sections.eli5: The old address form had too few boxes. This one adds more, so an address can be exact.

sections.title: Additional Civic Address Types
sections.content:
The RFC adds fourteen new fields, each tied to a civic address type number (CAtype) from RFC 4776. They cover places inside a building (BLD, UNIT, ROOM, SEAT), postal details (PCN, POBOX, ADDCODE), the kind of place (PLC) and a set of road elements (RD, RDSEC, RDBR, RDSUBBR, PRM, POM).

A full description of each type is in RFC 4776.
sections.eli5: New boxes on the form let you say which building, which room and even which desk.

sections.title: Thoroughfare Elements
sections.content:
A thoroughfare is a road, part of a road or other access route along which a final point is identified. In some countries a thoroughfare is split into sections whose street numbers repeat. The text's example is "West Alice Parade", with 5 sections each numbered from 1, so "7 West Alice Parade" could exist in 5 places. The RDSEC element names the section.

Minor streets can share a name and be told apart only by the major road they cross. RDBR (road branch) handles this, and may also be used where a major road is split into sections. RDSUBBR identifies a sub-branch of a branch.

A6 is retained for countries that need it, but where RFC 4119 used it for street names it MUST NOT be used any more; the RD element MUST be used for thoroughfare data.

Street numbering (HNO) applies to the most specific road element given, the first of RDSUBBR, RDBR, RDSEC or RD. The elements PRM, POM, PRD, POD and STS apply to the RD value only; qualifiers for branches MUST be in the RDBR or RDSUBBR text.
sections.eli5: Some long roads are cut into parts that each start numbering at 1. The new boxes say which part of the road and which side street you mean.

sections.title: Country, A1 and Whitespace Rules
sections.content:
The country element is now limited to two uppercase characters matching the alpha-2 codes of ISO 3166-1.

The A1 element holds the top-level subdivision within a country. Without a country-specific guide, the second part of the ISO 3166-2 code SHOULD be used, with the country code and hyphen dropped. The RFC's examples include <country>CA</country><A1>ON</A1> and <country>AU</country><A1>ACT</A1>.

Values now use the XML token base type instead of string, so whitespace is normalized and collapsed before processing. Extra spaces and line breaks around a value do not matter, though whitespace can still be kept using character references such as  .
sections.eli5: Countries are written with a two-letter code, and extra spaces and line breaks do not change the meaning of an address.

sections.title: Languages and Scripts
sections.content:
Every element except country and PLC may carry an xml:lang attribute. Those two hold language-neutral values. The separate script field from RFC 4776 is dropped in favour of an xml:lang value with a script subtag.

Each civicAddress element is RECOMMENDED to use one language only, or a consistent combination. To give a location in several languages, include multiple civicAddress elements in the PIDF-LO document; ones describing the same location SHOULD go in the same tuple.

Converting from the DHCP format, which allows repeated elements in different languages, needs one civicAddress per language, with language-independent elements copied into each. If the receiver's language preferences are known, such as from an Accept-Language header, a single address can be built by weighting the values and picking the highest.
sections.eli5: If an address is written in two languages, you write it out once in each language instead of mixing them in one form.

sections.title: Example Civic Address
sections.content: The RFC gives a sample document set in Australia. It uses country AU, A1 NSW, the road RD Flinders with STS Street, a branch RDBR Campbell Street, a landmark, a room, a place type and a P.O. box. The sample deliberately has odd spacing, which the token type normalizes away.
sections.eli5: The example is a filled-in form for a video rental store on a street corner.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The format is designed for inclusion in a PIDF-LO document, so it is subject to the same security considerations as RFC 4119. Use of the representation in other XML documents is outside the scope of this RFC.
sections.eli5: This form follows the same safety rules as the older location form, because it is used the same way.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC registers an XML namespace, urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:pidf:geopriv10:civicAddr, and an XML schema, urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:pidf:geopriv10:civicAddr. The schema is the entirety of Section 4 of the RFC.

It also updates the civic address type registry established by RFC 4776: the PIDF column of the CAtypes table now includes the new types listed in the RFC.
sections.eli5: The official lists were updated so the new address names have a registered home.
